title: Gateway model ids are endpoint names; unnamed endpoints are skipped and created_at is converted to seconds
answers: why does the OpenAI models list show the wrong id for an endpoint
model id in client.models.list() is not usable as the model parameter
created timestamp in the gateway models response is wrong or too large
which gateway endpoints appear in the OpenAI-compatible model list
body:
Invariant: the OpenAI-compatible model id is the gateway endpoint name, because /gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions routes on that name as the model parameter.
Enforced in mlflow/server/gateway_api.py:list_models: endpoints without a name are filtered out (`if endpoint.name`), and the result is sorted by name.
`created` is `endpoint.created_at // 1000`, so the store's millisecond timestamp becomes the seconds the OpenAI format expects (the test uses 1234567890123 -> 1234567890).
Breaks if skipped: unnamed endpoints appear with ids that cannot be used for routing, or timestamps are off by a factor of 1000.
Applies: changes to the response shape of /gateway/mlflow/v1/models or to the schema types in mlflow/gateway/schemas/models.py.
applies: Edits to the OpenAI-compatible models response or the gateway endpoint-to-model mapping.
says: The model identifier returned in the models list cannot be used for chat completions.
Model creation timestamps in the gateway model listing are showing in milliseconds instead of seconds.
Endpoints without names should not be displayed in the OpenAI compatible model catalog.
Make the AI gateway list endpoint names as model IDs sorted alphabetically.
search: The OpenAI-compatible model listing maps model IDs to gateway endpoint names so /gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions can route on that parameter. In mlflow/server/gateway_api.py:list_models, unnamed endpoints are filtered out, the list is sorted by name, and created_at timestamps are converted from milliseconds to seconds via integer division by 1000. This applies to changes to /gateway/mlflow/v1/models and schema types ModelObject and ResponsePayload in mlflow/gateway/schemas/models.py.
